title: Monte Carlo Simulation
description: Monte Carlo simulation estimates quantities by random sampling: instead of solving an integral or a probability analytically, the method draws thousands of random trials and averages the results. The demo estimates pi by throwing seeded darts at a unit square and counting how many land inside the quarter circle. Error shrinks with the square root of the sample count, which is why the demo's 200,000 samples land close to pi.
protocol: Define the quantity as an expected value over random draws.
Draw N samples with a seeded RNG for reproducibility.
Average the outcomes; report the estimate and its standard error.
Double N and confirm the error shrinks as expected.
Document the seed so anyone can reproduce the run exactly.

provenance: public-harvest: Monte Carlo method (Ulam/von Neumann); pi-estimation is the canonical demo.

title: Agent-Based Modeling
description: Agent-based modeling simulates a system as many small decision-making agents following simple rules, then watches large-scale patterns emerge. The demo runs a miniature Schelling segregation model on a grid: agents are happy when enough neighbors match them, unhappy agents move, and the grid is measured for clustering before and after. No central controller plans segregation — it emerges from the rules.
protocol: Define agent state, neighborhood, and the decision rule.
Initialize the population on a grid with a fixed random seed.
Step the model: unhappy agents relocate to random open cells.
Measure the emergent pattern (similar-neighbor fraction) over steps.
Sweep the happiness threshold to map rule-to-pattern sensitivity.

title: Discrete-Event Simulation
description: Discrete-event simulation models systems where state changes only at event moments — a customer arrives, a server finishes — and jumps the clock from event to event instead of ticking every second. The demo simulates a single-server queue (M/M/1): exponential arrivals, exponential service, seeded, measuring average wait and server utilization over 5,000 customers.
protocol: List the event types and the state they mutate.
Seed the RNG; schedule the first arrival.
Loop: pop the earliest event, advance the clock, process it, schedule follow-ups.
Collect statistics: waits, queue lengths, utilization.
Validate against the M/M/1 closed-form averages as a sanity check.

protocol: Name the stocks, flows, and feedback loops.
Write the differential equations for each stock.
Choose a step size small enough for stability; integrate.
Plot or tabulate the trajectory at regular marks.
Test loop dominance by knocking out one feedback at a time.

Assemble into the global system; apply boundary conditions.

title: Computational Fluid Dynamics (Stam Stable Fluids, 2D)

The demo runs a small 32x32 grid for 40 steps with a seeded emitter and reports total density (conserved-ish) and peak velocity, showing the plume advecting upward.
protocol: Store velocity and density fields on a staggered or collocated grid.
Advect: trace each cell backward along velocity (semi-Lagrangian).
Diffuse with an implicit solve; project to remove divergence.
Add sources (emitters, forces) each step.
Check invariants: density conservation, stability at large steps.

Tally state frequencies.

title: Quantum Circuit Simulation (State Vector)

protocol: Represent the 2^n state vector explicitly.
Apply gates as matrix operations on the vector.
Compute outcome probabilities via the Born rule.
Verify normalization after every gate.
